messages:
jordan: quick heads-up — after the 06:12 canary we saw ~3% spike in OOMs on p3. Pattern: FlashAttention path ends up invoking cuBLASLt for FFN, cuBLASLt asks for a workspace > available slab and we get hard OOMs instead of graceful fallback. logs attached below. :eyes:

lee: saw the same in telemetry. OOM spikes line up with KV cache churn when a few long-context requests hit mid-batch. batch mix looks like the trigger.

nina: sample log snippet from the worker: 
```
[2026-03-17T06:12:45Z] kernel: cublaslt_get_workspace_size -> requested 245M
[2026-03-17T06:12:45Z] allocator: slab_free 128M -> attempt allocate 245M -> OOM
[2026-03-17T06:12:45Z] kernel: fallback -> none (OOM)
```

samir: quick hypothesis: workspace estimator logic uses max(seq_len) but doesn't account for pad-to-multiple alignment + batchpad, so mixed-length batches underreserve. plus slab fragmentation from KV cache evictions reduces contiguous free. result = cublaslt asks for a contiguous chunk we don't have.

jordan: propose immediate mitigations: 1) add conservative per-kernel workspace headroom (e.g. +25%) for cuBLASLt requests, 2) proactive slab coalesce before launching heavy kernels, 3) change batcher heuristics to prefer homogeneous seq_len groups, 4) KV pre-evict policy for long-context spikes. I'll own 1+2, @lee take 3, @nina take 4.

lee: agree. For 3 we can bin by (seq_len rounded up to 32) then fill batches within a bin. Also cap allowed mixed-bin ratio. Pseudo: 
```python
# in batcher
bins = group_by(lambda r: ceil(r.seq_len/32)*32)
for b in bins:
    while b: yield b.pop_chunk(max_batch)
# allow a small mixed buffer for latency-sensitive short requests
```
We should start with mixed_ratio=0.08 and iterate.

nina: KV policy: when a request needs extra workspace and slab_free < requested+headroom, pre-evict oldest KV entries until free >= requested+headroom. Emit metric kv_evicted_bytes and kv_eviction_count. Also mark the request as "kv-evicted" in tracing.

samir: also add kernel-level soft cap: if cuBLASLt requests > (largest_contiguous_free - safety_margin) then force FlashAttention fallback (slower but memory-friendly) instead of attempting cuBLASLt which OOMs. That will turn some latency down but avoid hard failures.

perf-bot: microbench after local patch: p99 latency +0.3%, throughput -0.6% under uniform load; OOMs -> 0 on stress harness. Full traces at /tmp/perf/1717001111.patch.json

ci-bot: smoke CI for branch "ws-headroom-coalesce" -> green. added slab_coalesce_count metric to telemetry.

jordan: rollout plan: canary at 10% on p3 cluster with telemetry gates (OOM rate, p99 latency, batch_fill_rate, slab_fragmentation_ratio). check at +6h, +24h. ticket: https://rwd/infra/issue/INFR-4721 (tracking).

lee: I'll add a lightweight allocator exporter: slab_coalesce_count, largest_contiguous_free, slab_fragmentation_ratio. Also adding hist of workspace requests by kernel: ws_request_histogram (buckets: 4M, 16M, 64M, 256M, 1G).

nina: alert: kv_evicted_bytes rate > 5x baseline => page incident and rollback.

samir: small profiling tool I'll land: dump per-kernel workspace request histogram to /tmp/ws_hist.json for 24h on canary nodes. include seq_len, batch_size, kernel_choice. simple shim: 
```json
{"seq_len":512, "batch":8, "kernel":"cublaslt", "req":245000000}
```

jordan: cool. once patches are merged let's coordinate a 10% canary tomorrow 07:00 UTC. I'll open the PRs and link. :rocket:

lee: ack. will add canary dashboard panels for these new metrics.

nina: ack, adding tracing spans and annotation for when we evict KV during a request.

samir: small follow-up idea: opportunistic buffer reuse across concurrent short requests to reduce fragmentation — parking it in a separate RFC but could give big wins if fragmentation is main culprit.

jordan: sounds good. thanks all. follow-ups: PRs incoming, canary tomorrow, I'll post links in this thread.
